A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same D-RASP research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Transformer training, length-generalization and decompilation experiments, including benchmark results, pruning analyses and extracted programs in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds training-seed, pruning-stability and pipeline-stage results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The reparameterization, layer-normalization linearization, multistage pruning, MLP splitting and primitive replacement procedures remain unchanged. Expanded explanations and corrected projection notation do not introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 11 algorithmic tasks and 17 formal languages. The added analyses reuse existing coverage. Appendix J.8 corrects the sorting description to agree with the existing task definition and examples; it does not establish a changed dataset.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparison method is added or removed. The original-model comparisons and primitive-versus-regularization comparison remain; the new experiments examine seeds and stages of the existing pipeline.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce fixed-configuration comparisons, graph/program diversity measures, Pearson correlations conditional on matching computation graphs, and a greater-than-90% match-accuracy filter for pruning stability. Existing experiments retain their training budgets, length ranges and primary task/match-accuracy protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix E substantially expands supplementary analysis with training-seed sensitivity across eight tasks, pruning stability across 21 models, stagewise faithfulness, and primitive-use/MLP-splitting statistics. The earlier architecture, checkpoint, layer-normalization and training-length analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports ten separately trained models with different seeds for each of eight fixed task/configuration combinations, including success counts across seeds. v1 lacks this controlled repeated-training analysis. No confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–2 and program-specific scores remain unchanged. New Table 3 reports seven decompilations versus ten length-generalizing models for Unique Bigram Copy, and two versus zero for Binary Majority Interleave. Appendix E additionally reports pruning consistency for 17/21 models and stagewise match accuracies of 93%, 93%, 95% and 95%, substantially extending the findings.

T1.justification: v1 states exact Transformer/program equivalence under LLNA, although LLNA permits negligible behavioral change. v2 explicitly requires exact equality in Equation 5 for Theorem 3.2 and strengthens the appendix restatement accordingly. The constructions and proofs otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contribution: extracting interpretable D-RASP programs from trained Transformers and providing evidence that length-generalizing small models often implement simple programs. The new analyses do not redefine that contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds arguments interpreting some decompilation failures as evidence about learned mechanisms, while acknowledging possible failures despite an underlying short program. It also explains why different pruned graphs can yield the same program. Much of the expanded LLM-applicability discussion already appeared in v1's FAQ.

D1.justification: Table 3 documents the configurations used for the new seed study and the correlation-aggregation exclusions. Appendix J.8 corrects the misleading consecutive-integer condition in the sorting description. Existing implementation settings and repository access information are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning against logic translations, Tracr, Transformer Programs and circuit discovery remain unchanged. The separate Related Work section reorganizes existing discussion; additional main-text citations already appeared elsewhere in v1.

P1.justification: v2 adds an introductory roadmap, separates Related Work from Discussion, expands the FAQ, and makes targeted methodological clarifications and wording corrections. Most prose and the overall organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the seed-summary Table 3, renumbers the existing primitive table, and corrects Figure 1's projection label from q==k to inp==out. Existing plots and appendix visualizations are retained, with relocation and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The new stability and stage analyses make reliability more assessable, and the exact-equality restriction improves the theorem's precision. These provide a limited net improvement. However, the stronger interpretation of decompilation failures is not fully reconciled with Table 3's exceptions, including two decompiled Binary Majority Interleave models but no length-generalizing models.
